newsitem.title: USA: Cohen warns Congress that bases must be closed.
newsitem.headline: Cohen warns Congress that bases must be closed.

text.p: U.S. Defense Secretary William Cohen urged Congress on Friday to swallow bitter political medicine and close more military bases instead of deeply cutting forces to save money for modern weapons.

"It's all hemlock time now...These are painful things that have got to be swallowed," Cohen said in an interview with reporters on a new assessment of U.S. strategy and forces to be unveiled on Monday.

Cohen predicted there would be "fireworks" on Tuesday and Wednesday when he testifies to Congress on his recommendation in the quadrennial defense review to close more domestic military bases following four rounds of base closings approved earlier by lawmakers.

Defense officials have said that the review will seek a cut of only about 60,000 troops from the 1.4 million-member active duty forces in order to keep the armed forces advances around the world and ready to fight two wars at once. It will also seek cuts of about 75,000 in part-time reserve forces.

Cohen, who retired this year as a Republican senator from Maine, stressed that he had made tough and unpopular choices in the review because "I am not running for anything -- I don't have to do the politically-correct thing anymore."

"I will ultimately present them (Congress) with the choices I've had to make...Do you want the bases or do you want the most modern equipment in the hands of the future fighting force of the country?"
